at forudse.explanation: "At forudse" means "to foresee". It is built from "forud" (ahead) and "at se" (to see). To say you see a price rise coming: "Vi forudser en prisstigning" (We foresee a price increase).

at forudsige.explanation: "At forudsige" means "to predict". It is built from "forud" (ahead) and "at sige" (to say), so it is literally "to say ahead". To say someone predicts the weather: "Hun forudsiger regn i morgen" (She predicts rain tomorrow).

at forurene.explanation: "At forurene" means "to pollute". To say what harms the sea: "Olie forurener havet" (Oil pollutes the sea).

at forvandle.explanation: "At forvandle" means "to transform". To say something turns into something else, add "til" (into): "Heksen forvandlede prinsen til en frø" (The witch turned the prince into a frog). To say something changes by itself, add "sig" (itself): "Larven forvandler sig til en sommerfugl" (The caterpillar turns into a butterfly).

at forvente.explanation: "At forvente" means "to expect". To say you require something from someone: "Vi forventer, at du kommer til tiden" (We expect you to be on time).

at forvirre.explanation: "At forvirre" means "to confuse". To say that you are the one who is confused, use "forvirret" (confused): "Jeg er helt forvirret" (I am completely confused).

at forværre.explanation: "At forværre" means "to worsen". To say something becomes worse with nobody causing it, use "at blive værre" (to get worse): "Vejret bliver værre" (The weather gets worse).

at forårsage.explanation: "At forårsage" means "to cause". It comes from "en årsag" (a reason). To say what led to a result: "Ulykken forårsagede store forsinkelser" (The accident caused big delays).

at forære.explanation: "At forære" means "to give (as a gift)". To name the person receiving the gift, put the person right after the verb and leave out "til" (to): "Han forærede hende en ring" (He gave her a ring).

at fotografere.explanation: "At fotografere" means "to photograph". To say you take a picture of something, use "at tage et billede af" (to take a picture of): "Jeg tager et billede af huset" (I take a picture of the house).

at fremføre.explanation: "At fremføre" means "to present / put forward". To say you put forward a view: "Hun fremførte sine synspunkter" (She put forward her views). To say someone performs music before an audience: "Koret fremførte en salme" (The choir performed a hymn).

at fremhæve.explanation: "At fremhæve" means "to emphasize". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at hæve" (to raise), so it is literally "to raise forward". To say you point out what matters most: "Læreren fremhævede de vigtigste punkter" (The teacher emphasized the most important points).

at fremkalde.explanation: "At fremkalde" means "to cause / develop (film)". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at kalde" (to call). To say something brings on an effect: "Medicinen fremkaldte kvalme" (The medicine caused nausea). To say you develop photos from film: "Jeg fremkalder billederne i aften" (I am developing the pictures tonight).

at fremkomme.explanation: "At fremkomme" means "to emerge / appear". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at komme" (to come). To say someone comes up with a claim, add "med" (with): "Han fremkom med en ny teori" (He came up with a new theory).

at fremlægge.explanation: "At fremlægge" means "to present". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at lægge" (to put). To say a group puts a report before others: "Udvalget fremlagde en rapport om skolerne" (The committee presented a report about the schools).

at fremme.explanation: "At fremme" means "to promote / further". It comes from "frem" (forward). To say something helps health grow: "at fremme sundhed" (to promote health). To say something holds growth back, use the opposite, "at hæmme" (to hinder): "Kulden hæmmer væksten" (The cold hinders growth).

at fremskynde.explanation: "At fremskynde" means "to speed up". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at skynde" (to hurry). To say you make a decision happen sooner: "Vi vil fremskynde beslutningen" (We want to speed up the decision). To say a car goes faster, use "at accelerere" (to accelerate) instead: "Bilen accelererer hurtigt" (The car accelerates quickly).

at fremstille.explanation: "At fremstille" means "to produce / portray". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at stille" (to place). To say a text or picture shows someone in a certain way: "Avisen fremstiller ham som en helt" (The newspaper portrays him as a hero).

at fremvise.explanation: "At fremvise" means "to display / show". It is built from "frem" (forward) and "at vise" (to show). To ask someone to show you a picture, use "at vise" instead: "Vis mig billedet" (Show me the picture).

at fri.explanation: "At fri" means "to propose". To name the person you ask to marry you, add "til" (to): "Han friede til hende" (He proposed to her). The same spelling "fri" is also an adjective meaning "off work": "Jeg har fri i dag" (I am off today).

at frifinde.explanation: "At frifinde" means "to acquit". It is built from "fri" (free) and "at finde" (to find). To say a court finds someone guilty, use the opposite, "at dømme" (to convict): "Retten dømte ham for tyveri" (The court convicted him of theft).

at frigive.explanation: "At frigive" means "to release". It is built from "fri" (free) and "at give" (to give). To say a publisher puts out a book, use "at udgive" (to publish) instead: "Forlaget udgiver bogen i maj" (The publisher publishes the book in May).

at fritage.explanation: "At fritage" means "to exempt". It is built from "fri" (free) and "at tage" (to take). To name what someone is freed from, add "for" (from): "Han blev fritaget for gymnastik" (He was exempted from gym).

at frygte.explanation: "At frygte" means "to fear". To say you are afraid of something in everyday talk, use "at være bange for" (to be afraid of) instead: "Jeg er bange for hunde" (I am afraid of dogs).

at fryse.explanation: "At fryse" means "to freeze". To say you feel cold: "Jeg fryser" (I am cold; literally, "I freeze"). To say water turns to ice: "Vandet fryser" (The water freezes). Do not mix it up with "en fryser" (a freezer): "Maden ligger i fryseren" (The food is in the freezer).

at fuldende.explanation: "At fuldende" means "to complete". It comes from "fuld" (full). To say someone completes a work of art: "Hun fuldendte maleriet" (She completed the painting). To say a meeting simply ends, use "at afslutte" (to end) instead: "Vi afslutter mødet" (We end the meeting).

at fuldføre.explanation: "At fuldføre" means "to complete". It is built from "fuld" (full) and "at føre" (to lead). To say you complete a long race: "Han fuldførte maratonløbet" (He completed the marathon).

at fungere.explanation: "At fungere" means "to work / function". To say a machine does what it should: "Opvaskemaskinen fungerer ikke" (The dishwasher does not work). To say a person has a job, use "at arbejde" (to work) instead: "Jeg arbejder på et hospital" (I work at a hospital).

at fylde.explanation: "At fylde" means "to fill / take up space". To say you fill a container: "Jeg fylder glasset med vand" (I fill the glass with water). To say a thing takes up space: "Sofaen fylder meget" (The sofa takes up a lot of space). To say how old you turn on your birthday: "Jeg fylder 30 i dag" (I turn 30 today).

at fylde op.explanation: "At fylde op" means "to fill up". The "op" (up) adds that you fill something all the way to the top. To say you fill the fuel tank: "Jeg fylder tanken op" (I fill up the tank).

at fylde år.explanation: "At fylde år" means "to have a birthday". To say how old you turn, add the age: "Jeg fylder tredive år" (I am turning thirty). To say it is your birthday without naming an age, use "at have fødselsdag" (to have a birthday): "Jeg har fødselsdag i dag" (It is my birthday today).

at fyre.explanation: "At fyre" means "to fire (dismiss)". To say a boss dismisses an employee: "Chefen fyrede ham" (The boss fired him). To say you make a fire in a stove: "Vi fyrer i brændeovnen" (We light the wood stove).

at få.explanation: "At få" means "to get". To say you are allowed to do something, use it in "få lov" (to be allowed): "Jeg fik lov" (I was allowed). To go and fetch something, use "at hente" (to fetch) instead: "Jeg henter brød" (I am fetching bread).

at få besked.explanation: "At få besked" means "to be notified". To say you will tell someone, use "at give besked" (to let someone know): "Jeg giver dig besked" (I will let you know).

at få besøg.explanation: "At få besøg" means "to have visitors". To say you go to see someone yourself, use "at være på besøg" (to be visiting): "Jeg er på besøg hos min mor" (I am visiting my mother).

at få det bedre.explanation: "At få det bedre" means "to feel better". To wish a sick person well, say "God bedring!" (Get well soon!).

at få et barn.explanation: "At få et barn" means "to have a baby", literally "to get a child". To say you and your partner are going to have a baby: "Vi får et barn" (We are having a baby).

at få fat i.explanation: "At få fat i" means "to get hold of". To say you grabbed an object: "Jeg fik fat i rebet" (I grabbed the rope). To say you could not reach a person: "Jeg kunne ikke få fat i ham" (I could not get hold of him).

at få fri.explanation: "At få fri" means "to get off (work or school)". To say when you were allowed to leave: "Jeg fik fri klokken tre" (I got off at three o'clock). To say you decide to take a day yourself, use "at tage fri" (to take time off): "Jeg tager fri på fredag" (I am taking Friday off).

at få hjælp.explanation: "At få hjælp" means "to get help". Danish uses "hjælp" without an article after "brug for" (need): "Jeg har brug for hjælp" (I need help).

at få kolde fødder.explanation: "At få kolde fødder" means "to get cold feet". To say your feet are really cold, use "at have kolde fødder" (to have cold feet): "Jeg har kolde fødder" (My feet are cold).

at få lov til.explanation: "At få lov til" means "to be allowed to". To name what you are allowed to do, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg fik lov til at gå hjem" (I was allowed to go home).

at få lyst til.explanation: "At få lyst til" means "to feel like". To name what you feel like doing, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg fik lyst til at gå en tur" (I felt like going for a walk). To ask what someone feels like having, use "have lyst til" instead: "Har du lyst til en kop kaffe?" (Do you feel like a cup of coffee?)

at få nok.explanation: "At få nok" means "to have had enough". To say you cannot stand something any more: "Nu har jeg fået nok!" (Now I have had enough!) To ask whether someone has eaten enough: "Har du fået nok at spise?" (Have you had enough to eat?)

at få ondt af.explanation: "At få ondt af" means "to feel sorry for". To say you pity someone: "Jeg får ondt af hende" (I feel sorry for her). Do not mix it up with "at have ondt i" (to have pain in): "Jeg har ondt i maven" (My stomach hurts).

at få ret.explanation: "At få ret" means "to be proven right". To say events showed that someone was correct: "Hun fik ret" (She was proven right). To say someone is right at this moment, use "at have ret" (to be right): "Du har ret" (You are right).

at få styr på.explanation: "At få styr på" means "to get control of / sort out". To say something is already under control, use "at have styr på" (to have under control): "Nu har jeg styr på regnskabet" (Now I have the accounts under control).

at få tid.explanation: "At få tid" means "to find time": "Jeg fik tid til at læse" (I found time to read). To say you got an appointment, for example at the hairdresser: "Jeg fik tid hos frisøren" (I got an appointment at the hairdresser). To ask whether someone is free right now, use "at have tid" (to have time): "Har du tid nu?" (Do you have time now?)

related.en: to have time to / make it

at få travlt.explanation: "At få travlt" means "to get busy". To say you are busy right now, use "at have travlt" (to be busy): "Jeg har travlt" (I am busy).

at få øje på.explanation: "At få øje på" means "to catch sight of", literally "to get an eye on". To say you noticed an animal: "Jeg fik øje på en ræv" (I caught sight of a fox).

at føde.explanation: "At føde" means "to give birth". To say a woman has a baby: "Hun føder en datter" (She gives birth to a daughter). To say where you were born, use "at blive født" (to be born): "Jeg blev født i Aarhus" (I was born in Aarhus).

at fødes.explanation: "At fødes" means "to be born". It comes from "at føde" (to give birth). To say when you were born, use "at blive født" (to be born): "Jeg blev født i 1990" (I was born in 1990).

at føle.explanation: "At føle" means "to feel", as in sensing something with your body. To describe your mood, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg føler mig glad" (I feel happy).

at føle sig.explanation: "At føle sig" means "to feel (a certain way)". To say how you feel: "Jeg føler mig glad" (I feel happy). To say who is feeling, change "sig" to match the person: "du føler dig" (you feel), "han føler sig" (he feels).

at føles.explanation: "At føles" means "to feel (seem)". To say how a thing seems to you: "Vandet føles koldt" (The water feels cold). To say how a person feels, use "at føle sig" (to feel (a certain way)) instead: "Jeg føler mig træt" (I feel tired).

at følge.explanation: "At følge" means "to follow". To say someone walks behind you: "Hunden følger mig" (The dog follows me). To say you go along with someone to take them somewhere: "Jeg følger dig hjem" (I will walk you home).

at følge med.explanation: "At følge med" means "to keep up / come along". To ask whether someone can keep the pace: "Kan du følge med?" (Can you keep up?) To say you are joining someone: "Jeg følger med" (I will come along). Without "med" (along), "at følge" means "to follow": "Hunden følger mig" (The dog follows me).

at føre.explanation: "At føre" means "to lead / conduct". To say someone runs a conversation: "Han fører samtalen" (He is leading the conversation). To say you keep accounts or records: "Vi fører regnskab" (We keep the accounts).

en fabel.explanation: "En fabel" means "a fable". The word "fabelagtig" (fabulous) comes from it: "en fabelagtig rejse" (a fabulous trip).

en fabrik.explanation: "En fabrik" means "a factory". When "fabrik" is joined to another word, it gets an "s": "en fabriksarbejder" (a factory worker).

en fabriksarbejder.explanation: "En fabriksarbejder" means "a factory worker". It joins "fabrik" (factory) and "arbejder" (worker) with an "s". The ending "-arbejder" is also in "en havnearbejder" (a dock worker).

en facade.explanation: "En facade" means "a facade". It also means an appearance that hides what is behind it: "en facade af venlighed" (a facade of friendliness).

en fagbog.explanation: "En fagbog" means "a nonfiction book". It is built from "fag" (subject or trade) and "bog" (book).

en fagforening.explanation: "En fagforening" means "a trade union". It is built from "fag" (trade) and "forening" (association).

en faktor.explanation: "En faktor" means "a factor". To say something influences a result: "Pris er en vigtig faktor" (Price is an important factor). In math, a factor is a number that is multiplied: "2 og 3 er faktorer i 6" (2 and 3 are factors of 6).

en faktura.explanation: "En faktura" means "an invoice". To ask for the bill after a meal, use "en regning" (a bill) instead: "Kan vi få regningen?" (Can we have the bill?)

en familie.explanation: "En familie" means "a family". To say a couple starts having children, use "at stifte familie" (to start a family): "De vil stifte familie" (They want to start a family).

en familiefest.explanation: "En familiefest" means "a family party". It is built from "familie" (family) and "fest" (party). The word "fest" is also in "en julefest" (a Christmas party).

en fan.explanation: "En fan" means "a fan", as in a supporter of a team or singer. For a fan that cools a room, use "en ventilator" (a fan) instead: "Tænd ventilatoren, det er varmt" (Turn on the fan, it is hot).

en fange.explanation: "En fange" means "a prisoner". It comes from the verb "at fange" (to catch): a prisoner is a person who has been caught.

en fanklub.explanation: "En fanklub" means "a fan club". It is built from "fan" (fan) and "klub" (club).

en fantasi.explanation: "En fantasi" means "a fantasy". To say something is not real: "Det er bare en fantasi" (It is just a fantasy). It also means the ability to imagine things. To say someone has that ability: "Hun har en rig fantasi" (She has a rich imagination).

en far.explanation: "En far" means "a father". To speak to your own father, say "Hej, far!" (Hi, Dad!). The word "far" is also in "farfar" (father's father) and "farbror" (father's brother).

en farbror.explanation: "En farbror" means "an uncle (father's brother)". It is built from "far" (father) and "bror" (brother). To say your mother's brother, use "en morbror" (an uncle on your mother's side): "Min morbror bor i Odense" (My mother's brother lives in Odense).

en fare.explanation: "En fare" means "a danger". To say what may happen, add "for" (of): "Der er fare for brand" (There is a danger of fire). To say something is in danger, use "i fare" (in danger), without "en": "Dyret er i fare" (The animal is in danger).

en farfar.explanation: "En farfar" means "a grandfather (father's father)". It is built from "far" (father) and "far" (father). To say your mother's father, use "en morfar" (a grandfather on your mother's side): "Min morfar bor i Odense" (My mother's father lives in Odense).

en farmaceut.explanation: "En farmaceut" means "a pharmacist". To say what someone does for a living, leave out "en": "Min søster er farmaceut" (My sister is a pharmacist).

en farmor.explanation: "En farmor" means "a grandmother (father's mother)". It is built from "far" (father) and "mor" (mother). To talk to her or about her like a name, leave out "en": "Farmor kommer i dag" (Grandma is coming today).

en fart.explanation: "En fart" means "speed". To say things are moving fast and full of energy: "Der er fart på" (Things are really moving).

en fartbøde.explanation: "En fartbøde" means "a speeding ticket". It is built from "fart" (speed) and "bøde" (fine). To say you got a fine for something else, use "en bøde" (a fine): "Jeg fik en bøde" (I got a fine).

en fartgrænse.explanation: "En fartgrænse" means "a speed limit". It is built from "fart" (speed) and "grænse" (limit). To say someone goes over the limit: "at overskride fartgrænsen" (to exceed the speed limit).

en farve.explanation: "En farve" means "a color". The same spelling is also a verb, "at farve" (to dye): "Hun farver sit hår" (She is dyeing her hair).

en fase.explanation: "En fase" means "a phase". To talk about the moon, use the plural: "månens faser" (the phases of the moon).

en fastelavnsbolle.explanation: "En fastelavnsbolle" means "a Shrovetide bun". It is built from "fastelavn" (Shrovetide) and "bolle" (bun). Danes eat it around Fastelavn, a holiday in February or March when children dress up in costumes.

en faster.explanation: "En faster" means "an aunt (father's sister)". To say your mother's sister, use "en moster" (an aunt on your mother's side): "Min moster bor i Esbjerg" (My mother's sister lives in Esbjerg).

en favorit.explanation: "En favorit" means "a favorite". To make a word with it, put "favorit" in front of another word: "favoritsang" (favorite song).

en feber.explanation: "En feber" means "a fever". To say you have a fever, leave out "en": "Jeg har feber" (I have a fever).

en fejebakke.explanation: "En fejebakke" means "a dustpan". It is built from "feje" (to sweep) and "bakke" (tray). The word "bakke" also means "a hill": "en stor bakke" (a big hill).

en fejl.explanation: "En fejl" means "an error / bug". To say a program has a fault: "Der er en fejl i programmet" (There is an error in the program). To say a person did something wrong: "Jeg lavede en fejl" (I made a mistake).

en fejltagelse.explanation: "En fejltagelse" means "a mistake". It comes from "at tage fejl" (to be wrong). For a fault in a machine or a text, use "en fejl" (an error): "Der er en fejl i teksten" (There is an error in the text).

en fejring.explanation: "En fejring" means "a celebration". It comes from "at fejre" (to celebrate). To name what is celebrated, add "af" (of): "fejringen af jul" (the celebration of Christmas). To talk about the party itself, use "en fest" (a party): "Festen starter klokken otte" (The party starts at eight o'clock).

en ferie.explanation: "En ferie" means "a vacation". To say you are going away, use "på" (on): "Jeg tager på ferie" (I am going on vacation). To say when something happens, use "i ferien" (during the vacation): "I ferien læser jeg meget" (During the vacation I read a lot).

en fersken.explanation: "En fersken" means "a peach". To talk about more than one peach, add "-er": "tre ferskener" (three peaches).

en fest.explanation: "En fest" means "a party". To say you throw a party: "Vi holder fest i weekenden" (We are having a party this weekend). To wish someone a good time at a party, say "God fest!" (Have a good party!).

en festdag.explanation: "En festdag" means "a festive day". It is built from "fest" (party) and "dag" (day). To talk about a public holiday, use "en helligdag" (a public holiday): "Juledag er en helligdag" (Christmas Day is a public holiday).

en festival.explanation: "En festival" means "a festival". A big Danish example is "Roskilde Festival", a music festival held in Roskilde every summer.

en festsal.explanation: "En festsal" means "a banquet hall". It is built from "fest" (party) and "sal" (hall).

en festtale.explanation: "En festtale" means "a celebratory speech". It is built from "fest" (party) and "tale" (speech). To say someone gives a speech, use "at holde" (to hold): "at holde en tale" (to give a speech).

en fiasko.explanation: "En fiasko" means "a failure". Danish spells it with a "k" where English "fiasco" has a "c".

en figur.explanation: "En figur" means "a figure". To say a character in a story: "en figur i bogen" (a character in the book). To describe someone's body shape: "Hun har en flot figur" (She has a nice figure).
